newsitem.title: USA: Bankrupt retailer reports narrower loss.
newsitem.headline: Bankrupt retailer reports narrower loss.

text.p: Retailer Edison Brothers Inc. Monday reported slightly narrower second-quarter losses and said it was on target for emerging from bankruptcy next spring.

The St. Louis-based company, whose retail chains include the Oaktree and J. Riggings stores, reported a net loss of $25.2 million, or $1.14 a share, for the quarter ended Aug. 3. That compared with with last year's second-quarter loss of $25.7 million, or $1.17 per share.
Quarterly revenues dropped to $268.8 million from $334.7 million.

The results included a $7 million charge for restructuring and reorganization. The company, which filed for Chapter 11 protection from creditors last November while struggling with excess inventory, spent $20.9 million for those purposes in 1995's second quarter.
Edison President Alan Miller said the company is "on plan" to emerge from bankruptcy in the spring of 1997.
"We are encouraged by the initial results of the companywide initiatives," Miller said in a statement. "However, we're still in the middle of our restructuring phase."
The company said it was taking a number of steps to improve results, including improved training and new operating standards for every store, better merchandise and improving stores' appearance.

Edison Brothers reported higher losses for the six-month period compared with last year's first half. The company posted a loss of $42.9 million, or $1.93 a share, on revenues of $526.9 million compared with $32.1 million, or $1.46 per share, on revenues of $652.8 million last year.
Edison Brothers stock was unchanged at $1.875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

In addition to Oaktree and J. Riggings, the company operates the JW/Jeans West, Coda and Repp Ltd. Big & Tall menswear stores; Phoenix mens big and tall catalogu; 5-7-9 Shops junior apparel stores; and Bakers, Leeds, Precis and Wild Pair shoe stores.
